maml:description.maml:para: Exports configured Outlook Classic calendars, with named configurations and coordinated concurrent runs.

outcalget 0.3.6. One Windows PowerShell 5.1 file; no administrator rights, runtime modules/downloads, Graph permissions, endpoint exclusions or policy bypass. The native Outlook exporter preserves Full details, today through today + 29 LOCAL calendar dates inclusive, unrestricted working hours and saved privacy/attachment choices. Private details and attachments default to off during new setup. Existing schema-1 configurations from 0.1.x and 0.2.0 are accepted unchanged.

No -Profile means the existing default config.json. -Profile default selects that same file. -Profile team selects profiles\team.json beneath the existing local state root. A missing named profile fails with CONFIG_MISSING, exit 2: no default fallback and no setup prompt. -Configure -Profile team creates it after a successful test export. Named setup refuses an existing profile; use a new name to create another binding. -Config remains available for existing explicit configuration paths and cannot be combined with -Profile. Export profile names are NOT Outlook MAPI profile names; the configuration's profileName still binds the actual Outlook session.

Calendar setup offers (1) the original Outlook folder picker, (2) another mailbox's shared default Exchange calendar by full owner email, and (3) accessible calendars already added to Outlook's Calendar navigation list. Option 3 addresses shared/linked calendars absent from PickFolder. Only option 2 uses GetSharedDefaultFolder; it does not select arbitrary secondary shared calendars. Both paths use the same native GetCalendarExporter/SaveAsICal operation. Outlook sharing/export permissions apply. No email, invitation or sharing request is sent. For validated option-2 shared-default bindings, Outlook can return Folder.Store=null by design. This is accepted after Exchange owner identity has been revalidated; native Application Folders synchronization still runs before an owned-session export. A null Store on an ordinary folder binding or an explicit non-Exchange store fails cleanly instead of claiming synchronization. Each export additionally inspects the native CalendarSharing.Folder and uses NameSpace.CompareEntryIDs to verify that the exporter targets the resolved calendar before SaveAsICal. Shared mailbox identity pinning also uses CompareEntryIDs because different entry-ID representations can refer to the same object. Native folder bindings additionally retain store validation.

Internet availability is required, using Windows Network List Manager. When Outlook Classic is already open by the user, the helper attaches, performs no explicit sync and leaves it open. Otherwise it starts the machine-registered Classic installation in the saved MAPI profile for configured exports; interactive setup uses normal Outlook startup/default-profile behavior and can display its usual profile/sign-in dialogs. The helper waits for native readiness/online Exchange/group sync and requests normal Quit only for the exact process it started. Other exports can join that process. The creator waits for all joined usage leases before closing it; joined runs synchronize their own selected calendars and never request Quit themselves. Your ordinary configured Windows user must be logged on in the same desktop session. -NonInteractive cannot suppress Office sign-in/security dialogs. Logged-off/server Office automation and new Outlook are unsupported.

REQUIRED TASK SCHEDULER SETTINGS Create one task per export profile when you want calendars to run concurrently. General: configured ordinary user; Run only when user is logged on; Run with highest privileges OFF. Do not use SYSTEM, Password/S4U or Run whether user is logged on or not. Choose the desired trigger; use a 1-2 minute delay for an at-logon trigger.

Action = Start a program; substitute your approved absolute paths: Program/script: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe Add arguments: -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -STA -File "C:\ApprovedTools\outcalget.ps1" -Scheduled -Profile team -Debug Start in: C:\ApprovedTools Omit -Profile team for the original default calendar. Append -Config "C:\...\config.json" only for a legacy explicit configuration path, never alongside -Profile. No shell redirects, execution-policy switches, task registration or elevation are used.

For each task: If already running, Do not start a new instance. Different tasks can run concurrently with different profiles. Do not enable automatic failure retries. Optional Run as soon as possible after a missed start is suitable only while signed in and online. Do not require idle; allow battery execution and avoid battery-transition stops if needed. Do not wake the laptop by default. Sleep/logoff prevents export. Allow at least 60 minutes before Scheduler's external stop limit with the defaults, so several bounded coordination, worker and cleanup waits cannot trigger a hard stop. Increase that limit if you raise budgets or add many contending calendars; no duration is guaranteed for arbitrary contention. Network condition is optional: the script always checks Windows Internet status. An employer may restrict task creation.

CONFIGURATION AND CONCURRENCY State root: %LOCALAPPDATA%\osp\consulthelp\outcalget. Default: config.json. Named: profiles\<lowercase-name>.json. Names are case insensitive, 1-48 ASCII letters/digits/hyphens/underscores, starting with a letter/digit; reserved DOS device names are forbidden. Existing configurations are bound to Windows SID, Outlook MAPI profile and exact native folder identifiers. Shared-default bindings instead pin the resolved Exchange directory owner ID and save its canonical SMTP address; every worker resolves and checks that identity again. Mailbox/directory changes can require explicit reconfiguration. Configuration and operational state contain sensitive IDs.

Different output paths are mandatory. Persistent private output-claims\<hash>.json records reserve each physical filename for its canonical configuration path. The managed default/named catalog is also checked, protecting old unregistered configs. Explicit custom configs register claims when used; other unused custom config paths cannot be discovered. Copies/moves do not automatically transfer output ownership. A claim remains if a profile or output file is deleted, preventing accidental reuse. Failed new setup removes only its own new claim when the outcome is certain.

To deliberately retire a claim: finish all helper runs; review the protected record's configurationIdentity and outputIdentity; ensure every referencing task/configuration has been retired or redirected, then remove only that claim. Claims are not recovery markers and must not be routinely deleted. No automated reassignment is provided. Catalogs over 256 profiles and malformed managed configurations fail clearly.

Drive aliases are resolved through read-only Windows volume-GUID metadata. Hard-linked configuration/output/staging targets and reparse points are rejected. Output cannot be inside protected runs, locks, profiles, output-claims or default logs directories. The canonical destination is checked again immediately before publication. Existing conservative local fixed-NTFS/private-ACL/path-length rules are retained (see SECURITY).

Per-configuration, actual-calendar and output locks reject unsafe overlap with exit 6. Known native folder bindings and shared-owner bindings are reserved before startup. All Outlook COM worker operations are queued through one bounded gate: the script supports concurrently active runs; native Outlook calls are serialized. Short lifecycle coordination gates protect startup, sync membership and close decisions. Live parent PID/start-time/session checks plus shared usage handles prevent closing under another export. If the last usage lease cannot be confirmed released within the budget, Outlook is left open and recovery is required. One Outlook instance supports one MAPI profile; concurrent export profiles must use that same currently running Outlook MAPI profile. Install the same current script for all tasks. Upgrade only with no helper running; do not run older copies concurrently, since they do not implement these leases.

DATE WINDOW AND RECURRENCE (0.3.6): The run captures its local startup date through date + 29 inclusive: 22 October 2026 requests 22 October through 20 November 2026. IncludeWholeCalendar is false and native StartDate/EndDate are read back before SaveAsICal; mismatch fails with EXPORT_RANGE_MISMATCH, exit 4, before output replacement. A recurring VEVENT may retain its original September DTSTART and RRULE. That alone does not prove a wrong request. Native series/exceptions are preserved without flattening or clipping; importing a retained rule can yield occurrences outside the selected dates. Normal records and Json expose rangeStartDate, rangeEndDate and timeZoneId. See docs/outcalget/usage.md for inspecting date-only evidence privately.

STARTUP VISIBILITY (0.3.6): The launcher requests minimized Outlook. Scheduled additionally attempts Explorer.WindowState=olMinimized once for the exact newly started session during readiness; update-calendar forwards Scheduled. Existing/joined/user-active sessions are untouched and no Explorer is created. No periodic minimization or Office dialog suppression is performed. Record/Json outlookStartupWindow is not_requested, minimized, not_available, user_activity or unavailable; unavailable warns with OUTLOOK_MINIMIZE_UNAVAILABLE and export continues. Outlook can still flash or activate windows through native startup/add-ins/sign-in/security dialogs. PowerShell WindowStyle Hidden does not hide those dialogs. Windows focus behavior remains subject to target acceptance; see docs/outcalget/operations.md.

22 OCTOBER VERIFICATION: Synthetic date/read-back, recurrence preservation, owned startup/user-activity/lease guards, worker gating and normal-record checks pass on Linux PowerShell tooling. Actual Windows Outlook recurrence serialization, window focus/minimization, Exchange and Task Scheduler acceptance are NOT RUN here. The reported ICS itself has not been inspected.

Interactive source/options selection and a test export. Saves only after success and requires an unoccupied output filename. Never put this switch in a scheduled action. With -Profile, creates a new named configuration and refuses an existing named file. Starts Classic if closed, waits for its profile/stores and online Exchange, then offers selection. The selected calendar is synchronized before the test export when the session is script-owned. Existing user sessions are left open and receive no explicit sync. Only this run's owned startup process is eligible for normal Quit during cleanup.
Alias: -Profile. Names an export configuration; no selector or default reuses the original config.json. This never selects or changes the Outlook MAPI profile.
Legacy explicit absolute local .json path; mutually exclusive with -Profile.

Read-only business preflight of config/source/apparent path/output ownership. Requires already-open Outlook. No native export, output write, claim registration, explicit sync or freshness/consumer test. Operational logs, locks and private worker files can occur.
Non-prompting saved export plus scheduled metadata. Does not create a task or alter business behavior. Incompatible with Configure, Check, Help and Version parameter sets.

Default 300 seconds, range 15-1800. Applies to each catalog/lifecycle/COM-queue or joined-session cleanup wait. Worker queue time is additional to its native-work budget; parent monitoring detects native start separately and also enforces a total deadline. A busy same-configuration/calendar/output lock fails immediately rather than queuing.

Export-only readiness budget, default 120 seconds, range 15-600. Includes native COM, saved-source and primary online Exchange readiness for script-owned sessions; blocking COM work is isolated in a bounded worker process. Configure uses the embedded defaults.

Export-only native group synchronization budget, default 180 seconds, range 30-600. Applies to a process started here and to joined script-owned sessions. Existing user sessions receive no explicit sync. Native sync completion is not proof of freshness. Connection recovery shares this same budget, never a fresh timeout. At most three native starts are allowed; each interrupted attempt is stopped/detached and a new correlated completion is required after recovery. Explicit Work Offline fails promptly.
Absolute approved private local directory; default state-root\logs. Does not relocate configuration, ownership claims or operational state. Overrides the embedded log path.

One result JSON envelope on stdout, including handled failures. Schema 1 retains all existing fields and adds namedProfile, sourceType and joinedOwnedSession. Debug does not change it. Do not combine with WhatIf/Confirm, whose host output can corrupt JSON.
Compatibility alias for full Get-Help; also supports Get-Help and -?.
Prints 0.3.6 without Outlook access or run records.
None. Configurations are generated JSON data. Private worker switches are not public API.

Normal CLI: UTC phase feedback, export/check summary, sanitized error on stderr, warnings and run-record path. Native hosts can render information/warnings on stdout. -Json suppresses phase feedback and provides one result envelope. Nonzero exits distinguish failure. Output ICS bytes are native Outlook output, not manually constructed events.

maml:alert.maml:para: DOCUMENTATION PACKAGING, 12 OCTOBER 2026 Standalone execution requires no XML, Markdown or agent instruction files. Declared platform/application dependencies and runtime input/configuration still apply. The native .EXTERNALHELP directive is used only for detailed help. Without XML, native help falls back to generated parameter syntax. To retain detailed help, optionally deploy matching script/docs folders so ../docs/outcalget/outcalget-help.xml is available. Verification text below is historical; current extraction and standalone checks are recorded in docs/outcalget/verification.md.

RUN RECORDS Required unique bounded UTF-8 JSON records initialize before business work, checkpoint parent phases, and finish with completed=true on handled completion. Normal records include outcome, safe source/lifecycle flags and phases. Debug adds allowlisted host versions, script SHA-256, codes, HRESULTs and timings to the SAME record, without prompts. Synchronization diagnostics retain at most 24 changed connection observations: Offline, primary Exchange mode, elapsed milliseconds and attempt number. These describe the primary account, not an independent measurement of the selected shared mailbox/cache. No calendar content, owner addresses, native IDs, profile names, paths, tokens or raw exceptions/child output enter logs. The additive failurePhase field preserves the primary error stage even after synchronization restoration or Outlook closure. The result envelope intentionally gives outputPath and runLogPath. Share only a reviewed run record; do not share config/profile files, output-claims, runs, partial ICS files or calendar exports for debugging.

Retention attempts 200 closed records and 14 days, protecting active handles; inaccessible files remain with warnings. Required checkpoint failure stops later work. A completion log failure after publication reports exit 5 with published=true; a successful export is not undone. Optional debug enrichment cannot mask the primary result. A missing/incomplete record means UNKNOWN, including abrupt termination or Scheduler's external stop. An old calendar.ics may be stale after failure; correlate runId/time/completed/published/exitCode. Host binding, signing/policy/parse refusal and hard termination can precede any record.

RECOVERY Only owned child workers can be stopped for timeout; Outlook is never forced closed. Native work may continue after worker loss. Per-output and global COM .lock.pending markers plus the owned lifecycle marker block unsafe retries, including other profiles. Normal completed COM calls remove only their own marker while still holding the COM queue gate. Handled uncertain work leaves Outlook open and retains protected artifacts. An alive lifecycle marker with ready/closing phase can belong to normal concurrent work; its existence alone is not a failure. Never remove a marker while a helper is running.

To recover: close Outlook normally; ensure no outcalget parent/worker remains; inspect state-root\locks\*.lock.pending and their runId/time. Review runs\<runId>\sync\sync-state.json before deletion. If settingRestored=false, restore the selected folder checkbox in Outlook's Application Folders Send/Receive group to originalInclusion, or ask IT to do so. Multiple concurrent runs can have distinct recovery state; review every retained run involved. Then remove only the failed run's output/COM/lifecycle pending markers and, if needed, its runs\<runId> folder and .outcalget-<runId>.partial.ics stage. Leave ordinary .lock files, output-claims and final calendars intact. Old 0.2.0 lifecycle markers also require this review; they cannot be adopted as current live sessions. Rerun with -Debug. Do not clear recovery state while Outlook could still be writing.

SYNCHRONIZATION AND CLOSURE LIMITS Successful owned/joined runs report synchronization=group_completed and a readable synchronizationSummary in the run record; CLI success says Outlook synchronization completed. The backward-compatible freshness=not_verified field means that server/cache equivalence was not independently checked, not that the observed synchronization was skipped or failed. Existing user sessions can have stale cached sources despite Internet status; synchronization=existing_session_not_requested records that choice. Owned/joined sessions require Offline=false and full-item Exchange mode 600/700/800, include the selected folder temporarily in SyncObjects.AppFolders, observe correlated SyncStart/OnError/SyncEnd, and restore its original InAppFolderSyncObject value. Temporary nonready readings wait within the original sync budget. An interrupted attempt cannot authorize export after recovery: a fresh attempt must complete while full-item connection is observed. Attempts are capped at three. Work Offline modes 100/200, native sync errors and Internet loss fail promptly; no Outlook connection settings are changed. Persistent connected headers-only mode 500 is reported as OUTLOOK_HEADERS_ONLY; persistent other nonready states retain OUTLOOK_CONNECTION_LOST with the actual last mode/Offline flag. Repeated recovered interruptions report OUTLOOK_CONNECTION_UNSTABLE. Full connection without completion times out normally. A narrow C# ComEventsHelper bridge and STA message pump use documented Outlook event metadata. Only numeric sync errors are retained. Application Folders can be created by Outlook and other members can sync. Non-Exchange or unavailable sync sources fail clearly. No Namespace.SendAndReceive or MailItem.Send is called. A group completion cannot prove that every shared-calendar server change reached the cache. Test representative content.

Closure requires exact started PID/start time, one Outlook process in this desktop, no open items/additional explorers/inline drafts, released participant leases and a normal Quit followed by confirmed process exit. User activity or uncertain native work leaves Outlook open with nonzero status and recovery artifacts. Avoid using a script- started session during export; the user-activity check-to-Quit interval cannot be atomic. Abrupt parent termination cannot guarantee closure or setting restoration. Joined-run sync failure/cleanup uncertainty can also prevent the creator from safely closing.

SECURITY / COMPATIBILITY Windows PowerShell 5.1 Desktop STA, FullLanguage and Windows .NET Framework 4.5+ are required by the COM adapter. Existing policy must permit COM and the transparent Add-Type bridges; blocked initialization fails without fallback/bypass. No runtime packages, credentials, Graph or tenant consent are needed. The file is unsigned: use your employer's existing approved signing/deployment process. Worker processes execute this SAME unchanged file under the same user with NoLogo/NoProfile/NonInteractive/STA. Startup reads HKLM App Paths without modification. Configured exports pass only the quoted saved /profile name to Classic; interactive setup supplies no profile switch and records the running MAPI profile after readiness and calendar selection. No broad Office process kill, registry/ACL/policy change, endpoint enumeration/exclusion or self-elevation is performed.

Path metadata uses OPEN_EXISTING read-only kernel32 handles, volume-GUID final paths and file link counts; no backup privilege is enabled. Native Outlook sync and normal corporate monitoring can perform network activity. Internet gating uses Windows NLM IsConnectedToInternet, without helper HTTP/ping probes or overrides; corporate Windows status may report unavailable despite internal service access. This is a clean failure, not proof of Exchange reachability. Connectivity is checked before business work, during owned sync, before native save and publication, but can still disappear between checks.

Retained deployment boundary: fixed local NTFS, no UNC/removable/reparse/short-name paths, absolute paths <=230 characters, output directory <=165 for staging space, private user/SYSTEM/Administrators ACLs with creator/owner recognized. Unknown corporate ACL principals fail. These are this tool's conservative snapshot rules, not general Windows requirements; supporting managed exceptions needs explicit design and target testing. Output defaults to 25 MiB max (1-250), timeout 120 seconds (30-600). Size is checked after native export, not a disk quota. ICS validation is structural, not complete RFC/consumer fidelity. Local dates include earlier appointments today; Outlook handles private details.

UPGRADE AND ACCEPTANCE Replace only the script while no helper is running; existing configuration and scheduled default action remain valid. Do not reconfigure a working default just to upgrade. For a named calendar: run the Configure/Profile example; Classic starts if closed. Select the correct source/output; Check/Profile preflight, then Scheduled/Profile/Debug actual export. Confirm current completed=true, published=true, exitCode=0 plus a refreshed destination and correct full details, private/attachment choices and 30-date range. Inspect recurring, all-day, Unicode, shared/private and boundary events in the intended calendar consumer.

Test each task with Scheduler's Run, Last Run Result 0x0 AND its corresponding record/file; then a short temporary trigger while signed in. Test a locked desktop if required. Test user-open Outlook (left open), initially closed Outlook (started/synced/closed) and no Internet (failure preserves old file and never starts Outlook). Test two distinct profiles simultaneously with Outlook both open and closed: files stay separate; the startup creator closes only after both finish. Test a missing profile and duplicate output refusal. If a shared navigation binding cannot reopen after Classic restarts, try the shared-default owner option for default calendars; secondary provider-specific calendars can remain unavailable and fail explicitly. Do not replace native folder opening with cache scraping.

FUNCTIONAL ACCEPTANCE FOR A SHARED CALENDAR A completed synchronization group or exit 0 alone does not prove server freshness or event completeness. After setup, inspect the actual generated .ics for a known appointment unique to that shared calendar within the next 30 local dates, checking its date/time and details. Compare with a manual full-details Outlook export using the same window; include recurring and all-day appointments when present. A valid empty file is allowed for a genuinely empty window, so check expected content rather than treating a nonzero event count as a source guarantee. Development fixtures exercise source routing and publication, not real Exchange event data.

ENGINEERING / VERIFICATION, 4 OCTOBER 2026 This revision retains native export semantics and schema-1 parsing; schema 2 is exact and conditional on sourceType. Pure business preflight and WhatIf remain distinct from export. ShouldProcess gates parent mutations; operational diagnostic I/O is the disclosed preview exception. Internal helpers do not introduce independent confirmation flows.

Local complexity/length exceptions remain on the existing parser/validation/native worker/ entry transaction and coherent ownership/recipient/navigation/setup/progress helpers. Four-space indentation and at most six internal parameters are retained; no claim that all default complexity/nesting/80-line budgets pass is made. The COM worker combines acquisition/export/reply/reference lifetime to preserve the common native operation. No blanket analyzer suppression is used; the narrow Framework Windows.Forms compatibility exception documents its explicit assembly load. Development tests/fixtures are not shipped.

PASS: PowerShell 7.4.6 parser and PSScriptAnalyzer 1.24.0 default rules plus PSUseCompatibleSyntax (5.1), PSUseCompatibleCommands and PSUseCompatibleTypes against win-48_x64_10.0.17763.0_5.1.17763.316_x64_4.0.30319.42000_framework, with zero issues outside the documented narrow explicit Windows.Forms load exception. PASS (0.3.2 baseline): 285 executable development checks on Linux/PowerShell 7.4.6: 48 portable regressions; 9 log/scheduler checks; 16 native-settings/protocol/queue-budget checks; 32 event/readiness/ownership checks; 32 baseline CLI checks; 21 lifecycle CLI checks; 58 profile/shared/navigation/path-identity/lease/help checks; 57 profile/concurrent-worker process checks; 12 setup readiness/feedback/native argument checks. They cover native settings, Gregorian dates, byte-preserved old configs, named setup/reuse/failure, shared resolution/identity/permissions, safe diagnostics, output collision/claims/aliases, queued native calls, same-calendar overlap, joined startup/sync/closure, closed-session setup, setup cancellation/known failure, joined setup/export lifetimes, shared null-Store synchronization/restoration/failure diagnostics, and recovery after abrupt worker loss. Child processes, private transactions and file-sharing handles execute; Windows/Outlook/ACL/connectivity/native path reads/events are simulated. Argument dispatch executes to a harmless fixture child; its start-time identity is simulated because it is unavailable in this sandbox. Actual C# path bridge compilation and native struct layout are checked; this does not execute kernel32 or prove Windows metadata behavior. PASS (0.3.3 historical focused): 124 checks rerun on that revision: 64 profile/shared/source-identity checks and 60 parent/worker process checks. Native source-folder matching, equivalent entry IDs, shared-source-dependent synthetic ICS contents, and refusal to publish/save wrong-source results are covered. The complete 0.3.2 suite was not rerun then. Outlook and Windows boundaries remain simulated. Parser/analyzer/BOM/CRLF/version/help were checked on the final file. PASS (0.3.4 historical focused): 130 checks on that revision: 47 synchronization/readiness/ownership logic checks; 20 native-settings/worker-protocol/queue-budget audit checks; 63 profile/ concurrent parent-worker process checks. Tests exercise interrupted sync recovery, discarded completion during disconnection, headers-only and Work Offline states, Internet loss, failed cleanup, three-attempt cap, one original deadline, bounded safe state observations and malformed-diagnostic refusal. Failed shared export/setup preserves existing bytes or remains unsaved; recovery diagnostics survive owned Outlook cleanup. The callback state machine executes with simulated COM events/message pumping; process fixtures execute real parent/workers and file transactions with Windows/Outlook boundaries simulated. Their wait fixture supplies chosen sync outcomes, so those process checks do not establish real Exchange recovery. The complete historical suite was not rerun. PASS (manual): profile/default compatibility, common native exporter settings, bounded process/COM ownership and output claims, ShouldProcess, allowlisted diagnostics, declared side effects and local complexity exceptions. UTF-8 BOM/CRLF checked before saving. Function/entry complexity was reviewed using AST-guided branch/loop/catch/logical counts and manual ownership review; no claim of threshold compliance, coverage percentage, duplication percentage or secret-scanner certification is made. NOT RUN: Windows PowerShell 5.1 execution, actual Outlook shared/navigation providers, Exchange freshness/SyncEnd/Quit, locked desktop, Task Scheduler, Windows NLM/ACL/NTFS, volume-GUID/drive-alias/hard-link behavior on Windows, architecture combinations, endpoint acceptance or consumer fidelity. No Windows/Outlook environment is available. USER-REPORTED PASS (0.3.0, one corporate laptop): legacy default export with Classic initially closed completed successfully. USER-REPORTED FAIL (0.3.0): named Configure with Classic closed stopped with OUTLOOK_NOT_RUNNING; the attached sanitized log confirmed that setup incorrectly used the already-open read-only path. Revision 0.3.1 adds owned startup and bounded setup readiness, retains selected-calendar sync before test export, preserves initial-state diagnostics across setup/export entry, and clarifies synchronization feedback. Target execution of this fix remains NOT RUN here. USER-REPORTED FAIL (0.3.1): shared-default selection and readiness succeeded, then sync failed reading ExchangeStoreType from a null Folder.Store. Microsoft documents this null value for GetSharedDefaultFolder. Revision 0.3.2 accepts it only for a validated shared-default Exchange binding; retains native sync/checkpoint/restoration; records the failure stage before cleanup; and reports sourceType before path validation. Process fixtures now execute the actual synchronization adapter with null-Store shared folders instead of bypassing it. Target Windows execution remains NOT RUN here. Revision 0.3.3 additionally audits the remote lookup/export route, replaces direct shared owner-ID string comparison with documented MAPI CompareEntryIDs, and checks CalendarSharing.Folder against the resolved source before any native output write. Mismatch/unidentifiable sources cannot publish output or complete setup. Tests include equivalent-ID representations, wrong-source refusals and source-dependent synthetic ICS payloads. These checks do not prove real provider event completeness or freshness. USER-REPORTED FAIL (0.3.3): the supplied run reached shared-default lookup, source readiness and native sync start, then our single-reading connection guard failed in sync-wait with OUTLOOK_CONNECTION_LOST. No native ICS export was attempted. The record contains earlier primary mode 700 but omits the actual mode/Offline at failure; transient recovery versus persistent connection loss cannot be inferred from that log. Revision 0.3.4 adds bounded recovery with a fresh required sync attempt, records actual connection transitions on success/failure, and preserves Internet/full-details gates. This fixes premature failure on recoverable states; it does not claim the unrecorded state was transient or that the target shared export has now passed. Target Windows, Exchange and Task Scheduler execution remains NOT RUN here. Revision 0.3.5 retains an interrupted attempt's event listener until correlated completion after Stop, before subscribing a replacement. Cleanup uses only the remaining original synchronization budget and fails closed if completion is absent. This prevents queued cancellation from contaminating the replacement; cancellation or other errors on an active attempt still fail. Ten address-free deterministic regressions pass on Windows PowerShell 5.1, with Outlook events simulated. Actual shared-calendar export/content acceptance remains unverified for this revision. No production certification is claimed. Test fixtures, frameworks and additional implementation files are not delivered.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Classic starts automatically if closed. Choose option 3 for a calendar already in the Calendar navigation list, or option 2 for a shared mailbox's default calendar. Choose a distinct output path. Later runs do not ask for a calendar, owner, options or output path.
Exports the existing default configuration without reconfiguration.
Headless named export. Use the same arguments in that profile's Task Scheduler action.
Read-only preflight. Outlook must already be open. Does not replace a real export test.
Preview: no source access, export, startup, output claim or configuration changes. Minimal run logging may occur; retention is skipped. Configuration/source is not validated.
